summary: Dario Amodei, a Princeton-trained biophysicist, worked at Baidu and Google Brain and was OpenAI's vice president of research before leaving to co-found Anthropic with his sister Daniela and other former OpenAI staff in 2021. In 2025 Trump's AI czar David Sacks accused Anthropic of "regulatory capture"; in February 2026, after Anthropic refused to drop limits on military uses such as mass surveillance and autonomous weapons, Trump ordered agencies to stop using its technology and the Pentagon labeled it a supply-chain risk, which Anthropic is challenging in court.

connections.name: Sam Altman
connections.description: Amodei worked at OpenAI from 2016, rising to vice president of research, then left with others over directional differences to found Anthropic in 2021. The two companies are now direct competitors: in February 2026 Altman called Anthropic's Super Bowl ads "clearly dishonest" and the company "authoritarian".

connections.name: Donald Trump
connections.description: On February 27, 2026 Trump ordered every federal agency to stop using Anthropic's technology, calling it a "radical Left AI company", after Anthropic refused to lift limits on uses such as mass surveillance of Americans and autonomous weapons. Amodei challenged the resulting Pentagon designation in court and apologized for a leaked internal memo criticizing the administration. In August 2026 U.S. District Judge Rita Lin voided the Pentagon’s supply-chain-risk designation, per the Daily Caller; a separate challenge was still pending.

connections.description: In October 2025 Sacks, then Trump's AI czar, accused Anthropic of a "sophisticated regulatory capture strategy based on fear-mongering"; Amodei answered with a statement correcting what he called inaccurate claims about Anthropic's policy positions.

connections.name: Pete Hegseth
connections.description: Defense Secretary Hegseth designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk to national security in February–March 2026; Anthropic sued, and Amodei said the ban was narrower than Hegseth had threatened. In August 2026 U.S. District Judge Rita Lin voided the Pentagon’s supply-chain-risk designation, per the Daily Caller; a separate challenge was still pending.
